questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the scheme given below, $X$ and $Y$, respectively, are

$\text{Metal halide}\overset{aq . NaOH}{\to}\text{White precipitate}\left(P\right) + \text{Filtrate}\left(Q\right)$

$P\mathop{\overset{aq . {H}_{2}{SO}_{4}}{\overset{{PbO}_{2} ( excess )}{⟶}}}_{heat}X\left(\text{a coloured species in solution}\right)$

$Q\mathop{\overset{MnO ( OH{)}_{2}, Conc . {H}_{2}{SO}_{4}}{⟶}}_{warm}Y\left(\text{gives blue-coloration with}KI - \text{starch paper}\right)$
questions.solution:
The metal halide can be manganese dichloride. It gives white precipitate of manganese hydroxide.

${MnCl}_{2}\overset{aq . NaOH}{\to}\mathop{Mn{\left(OH\right)}_{2}}_{\left(P\right)} + \mathop{NaCl}_{\left(Q\right)}$

The white precipitate manganese hydroxide on reaction with lead dioxide and concentrated sulphuric acid gives purple coloured solution permanganate.

$Mn{\left(OH\right)}_{2}\mathop{\to}_{Conc . {H}_{2}{SO}_{4}, heat}^{{PbO}_{2}\left(excess\right)}{MnO}_{4}^{-}\left(purplesolution\right)$

The sodium chloride gives ${Cl}_{2}$ on reaction with $MnO{\left(OH\right)}_{2}, conc . {H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$. The chlorine formed can oxidise iodide to iodine which gives blue colouration with starch paper.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Reduction of the metal centre in aqueous permanganate ion involves
options:
three electrons in neutral medium

five electrons in neutral medium

three electrons in alkaline medium

five electrons in acidic medium
questions.solution:
In neutral medium: $\quad \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{MnO}_2\left(\mathrm{Mn}^{7+}+3 e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{4+}\right)$
In alkaline medium : $\quad \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{MnO}_2\left(\mathrm{Mn}^{7+}+3 \varepsilon^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{4+}\right)$
In acidic medium : $\quad \mathrm{Mn}_4^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}\left(\mathrm{Mn}^{7+}+5 e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}\right)$

questions.q: Paragraph: When a metal rod $M$ is dipped into an aqueous colourless concentrated solution of compound $\mathrm{N}$, the solution turns light blue. Addition of aqueous $\mathrm{NaCl}$ to the blue solution gives a white precipitate $\mathrm{O}$. Addition of aqueous $\mathrm{NH}_3$ dissolves $\mathrm{O}$ and gives an intense blue solution.Question: The metal $\operatorname{rod} M$ is
questions.solution: Appearance of blue colour on addition of the metal rod $M$ to the solution of $N$ is an indication that metal may be $\mathrm{Cu}$. Later formation of white precipitate on addition of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and dissolution of this precipitate in aqueous ammonia confirm that while preipitate is of $\mathrm{AgCl}$. This implies that the solution $N$ is of $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$. This confirm that the metal $M$ is only $\mathrm{Cu}$.
